findings.title: Raw recovery codes are persisted in user storage
findings.body: The user-storage path serializes and passes `generatedCodes`, which are the plaintext recovery codes, as the credential challenge response. The local recovery-code credential model stores hashed code values, but an accepting user-storage provider receives and will commonly persist this plaintext JSON (as the added compatibility provider does). This gives anyone with access to the external user store reusable recovery codes, unlike the existing local-storage behavior. Pass a representation containing the hashed recovery-code data (and require validation to hash incoming codes), rather than the generated plaintext list.

findings.title: Recovery codes accepted by the user-storage implementation are never consumed
findings.body: The recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted value occurs in the stored list and never removes or marks that value used. Consequently the same recovery code can authenticate repeatedly for this user-storage path. Recovery codes are one-time credentials; this provider needs to atomically consume the matching code on successful validation, and the integration test should attempt a second login with the same code and assert that it fails.
